title: Dependent Queries
description: Chain queries that depend on each other using the enabled option for sequential data fetching.

data.text: **Dependent queries** (also called sequential queries) are queries that require data from a previous query before they can run. The key mechanism is the **enabled** option â€” set it to false until the prerequisite data is available, then set it to true to start the dependent query.

The enabled option is a boolean that controls whether useQuery executes its queryFn. When false, the hook does nothing â€” it does not fetch, not error, not show loading. When it becomes true (either from the start or via a reactive dependency), the query runs normally.

data.title: enabled with a Prop Dependency
data.content: Using enabled to control when a query starts based on component props

data.caption: How two dependent queries execute sequentially using the enabled flag
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Component mounts
    userId = '42'] --> B[Query 1 enabled: true
    queryKey: ['user', '42']]
    B --> C[Fetch user from server]
    C --> D[User data in cache
    user.id = '42']
    D --> E[Query 2 enabled becomes true
    queryKey: ['posts', '42']]
    E --> F[Fetch posts for user 42]
    F --> G[Posts data in cache]
    G --> H[Render user + posts UI]

    I[userId = null] --> J[Both queries disabled
    enabled: false]
    J --> K[Show 'Select a user' prompt]

    L[userId changes to '99'] --> M[Query 1 refetches
    for new user]
    M --> N[Query 2 refetches
    for new user's posts]

data.title: When to Use Dependent Queries
items: **Nested resources**: Fetch a user, then fetch their posts â€” posts depend on user.id
**Auth-dependent data**: Fetch the current user, then fetch their private settings
**Search then detail**: Fetch search results, then fetch details for the selected item
**Form with options**: Fetch a list of categories, then fetch products filtered by the selected category
**Multi-step wizards**: Step 2 data depends on the selection made in Step 1

data.text: You can also use data from one query inside another query's queryFn. React Query's cache ensures the prerequisite data is available. This pattern is useful when the second query's parameters depend on the first query's result.

data.title: Using First Query's Data in the Second QueryFn
data.content: Accessing cached data inside a dependent query's queryFn

data.title: Avoid Query Key Dependencies on Data
data.text: Never use data values (not just IDs) directly in a queryKey â€” only use stable identifiers like IDs. If the data object reference changes on every render, the query will refetch infinitely.

Each dependent query handles its own errors independently. If the first query fails, the second query never runs (enabled remains false). If the first query succeeds but the second fails, the first query's data remains in the UI while you show the second query's error.

data.title: Error Handling in Dependent Queries
data.content: Displaying partial data when one query in a chain fails

terms.definition: A boolean option on useQuery that controls whether the queryFn runs. When false, the query does not execute, does not error, and shows no loading state.
A query that relies on the result of another query before it can run. Implemented using the enabled option to delay execution until prerequisite data is cached.
Fetching data in a specific order where each step depends on the previous step's result. Contrasts with parallel fetching where all queries run simultaneously.

data.title: Build a Project Detail View
data.description: Create a ProjectDetail page that loads a project, then loads its team members and recent activity â€” each depending on the previous query's result.
steps: Create mock API functions: fetchProject(id), fetchTeamMembers(projectId), fetchRecentActivity(projectId)
Create ProjectDetail component accepting a projectId prop
Query 1: Fetch project with queryKey ['projects', projectId]
Query 2: Fetch team members with queryKey ['projects', projectId, 'team'], enabled: !!project
Query 3: Fetch recent activity with queryKey ['projects', projectId, 'activity'], enabled: !!project
Show loading state only for each query independently â€” project name appears as soon as Query 1 resolves
Handle errors for each query separately with distinct error messages
Style with Tailwind: project name as heading, team as avatar list, activity as a timeline
data.expectedOutcome: A project detail page where the header appears first, followed by team members and activity. Each section loads independently, and errors in one section do not block the others.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Dependent queries use the enabled option to control execution order
Set enabled: false until prerequisite data is available in the cache
The second query reads the first query's result from the cache via its queryKey
Each query handles its own errors independently
Use case IDs (not full objects) in dependent query keys for stability
Dependent queries are perfect for nested resources and multi-step workflows
data.takeaway: The enabled option is the simplest and most powerful tool for chaining queries â€” it turns independent hooks into a coordinated data-fetching pipeline.
